title: Becoming and Staying a Licensed Massachusetts Pharmacist
topic: Licensure / Pharmacist licensure, renewal and status changes
subtopic: Entry by examination or reciprocity under 247 CMR 3.00, application mechanics, the biennial renewal cycle and lapse ladder in 247 CMR 4.02, retired status, duplicate certificates and the 247 CMR 20.03 change-reporting duties
learning_objectives: Distinguish the examination pathway in 247 CMR 3.01 from the reciprocity pathway in 247 CMR 3.02, and state what each one requires that the other does not.
Apply the one-year linkage window in 247 CMR 3.01(7) and explain which examination score is actually at risk when it expires.
State who evaluates a reciprocity application first and who makes the final determination of eligibility.
Work out what a completed licensure application must contain and what follows when it is incomplete.
Place a lapsed personal registration on the 60-day and two-year ladder in 247 CMR 4.02 and name the consequence attached to each rung.
Say what retired status permits, what it forecloses, and what it does not shield the licensee from.
Run a set of facts against the four individual reporting duties in 247 CMR 20.03 and apply the single 14-calendar-day period to each.
State the two qualifiers that condition the protection in 247 CMR 3.05 and the licensure decisions it reaches.

orientation.text: A Massachusetts pharmacist licence is issued by the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, and almost every question in this area resolves into asking what the Board requires or what the Board decides. There are two doors into the licence. 247 CMR 3.01 is the examination door, used by an applicant who is not already licensed as a pharmacist elsewhere. 247 CMR 3.02 is the reciprocity door, used by an applicant who can prove licensure by examination in another state or jurisdiction and good standing in every state where the applicant holds a licence. The two doors have different entry conditions, but they converge on the same two substantive requirements: a documented pharmacy internship and a passing MPJE score. Reciprocity is not a paperwork transfer that carries an out-of-state licence across the state line intact.

On the examination pathway 247 CMR 3.01(1) and (2) state the same four-part shape twice. Both versions require the applicant to be 18 years of age or older by the scheduled date of the examination applied for, to have completed a pharmacy internship in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1), and to be of good moral character. What differs between them is the academic credential. A graduate of a college or school of pharmacy accredited by the ACPE or approved by the Board satisfies it with a doctor of pharmacy degree. A graduate of a non-approved college or school satisfies it instead with official Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Committee certification from NABP, an official copy of the FPGEC certificate submitted to the Board, and official notification of that certification received by the Board from NABP. The substitution is credential for credential. It does nothing at all to the internship requirement, which appears in both lists in identical terms.

Eligibility only gets the applicant as far as the examinations. 247 CMR 3.01(4) and (5) require passing both NAPLEX and MPJE with a score of not less than 75% on each, and 247 CMR 3.01(6) allows re-examination on either or both on a new application to the Board or a Board-approved testing service with all required fees. The provision that actually decides examination questions is 247 CMR 3.01(7), and it is not a cap on attempts. An applicant who fails one examination has one year from the administration date of the original examination to reapply to sit the failed one, and that year is the condition on which both examination scores are considered together. Let it run out and the passed score stops carrying: the applicant must apply to retake both NAPLEX and MPJE. Read that way, the clock is a shelf life for the score already earned, so the thing put at risk by delay is the examination the applicant had already passed.

The reciprocity door in 247 CMR 3.02 opens only if the other state or jurisdiction requires a degree of competency equal to that required of applicants in Massachusetts and the Board recognises that jurisdiction for purposes of licensure by reciprocity. The applicant files a preliminary application with NABP, and NABP, as agent of the Board, conducts the preliminary evaluation of the applicant's qualifications. Agent is the operative word. 247 CMR 3.02(1)(b) gives the Board the final determination of any applicant's eligibility, and 247 CMR 3.02(1)(a) lets an applicant whom NABP has notified that she does not meet the requirements request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision. An approved reciprocity application is valid for one year after the date of approval by NABP. The requirements themselves still include documentation of internship experience, a passing score of at least 75% on the MPJE, and personal appearance before the Board if requested; for a graduate of a non-approved school the Board must in addition receive an official copy of the applicant's FPGEC certificate from NABP.

Underneath both doors sits a set of application mechanics that decides more questions than its dullness suggests. Under 247 CMR 3.01(3) a completed application for examination must be fully and correctly completed by the applicant and must include a recent passport-size photograph showing the applicant's likeness, a certified birth certificate or other sufficient proof of place and date of birth, written notification to the Board or the Board's designee in the case of a name change, and payment of all required fees unless waived in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B. Two consequences follow, and they work together. 247 CMR 3.01(8) lets the Board refuse to consider any application that has not been properly completed, so an incomplete application is not something the Board is obliged to cure or to chase. And 247 CMR 3.01(9) makes all fees submitted in connection with a licensure application that the Board has reviewed and acted upon non-refundable, with the same non-refundability stated for reciprocity applications at 247 CMR 3.02(1)(d). Refusing to consider an application is still acting on it, which is why the fee does not come back.

Getting the licence and keeping it are separate problems, and the second one runs on a fixed calendar rather than on the licensee's own anniversary. Under 247 CMR 4.02(1) all personal registrations expire on December 31st of each even-numbered year and shall be renewed prior to January 1st of the following year if the registrant intends to continue practising pharmacy. 247 CMR 4.02(2) lets a registrant who did not renew before the expiration date renew on payment of an annual licence fee, applicable back licence fees and a late fee, and 247 CMR 4.02(3) states the price of practising in the meantime: any practice of pharmacy after the expiration of the personal registration constitutes the unlicensed practice of pharmacy and is subject to the penalties established for it. Paying is a step in renewing, not a renewal. The ladder then lengthens with the lapse. Failure to renew for more than 60 days, where the registration was not suspended or revoked, means renewal on satisfying conditions imposed by the Board, which may include the completion of additional contact hours of continuing education. Failure to renew for more than two years, again where the registration was not suspended or revoked, means taking and passing the MPJE and meeting all other conditions determined by the Board.

Two boundaries around that ladder are worth fixing early, because both are places where a neighbouring rule is easy to import by accident. The first is the qualifier that 247 CMR 4.02(4) and (5) each carry in their own text: they govern an applicant whose personal registration has not been suspended or revoked by the Board. A registration that was suspended or revoked travels a different route back, and that route is not taught in this section. The second is that 247 CMR 4.02 is only the renewal and lapse half of 247 CMR 4.00. Continuing education appears here only as something the Board may require more of after a lapse of more than 60 days; the continuing education requirement itself, with its own hour structure, programme approval and recordkeeping, is a separate subject and is deliberately outside the scope declared for this section.

Three smaller regimes finish the picture, and in each of them the intuitive answer is the wrong one. 247 CMR 3.04 lets a licensee whose licence is not surrendered, suspended or revoked petition the Board to place it on retired status, on demonstrating an intent to retire permanently from active practice in the Commonwealth and in all other jurisdictions. Retired status is expressly nondisciplinary, and it is expressly not a shelter: a licensee with retired status may not practise, the Board may decline to review any petition for reinstatement or return to current status, and nothing in 247 CMR 3.04 prevents the Board from initiating, pursuing or taking a disciplinary action against a retired licensee. 247 CMR 3.03 governs the duplicate certificate of licensure, the wallet card, which is requested on a Board-approved form with the required documentation; when the original resurfaces it is the duplicate, not the original, that shall be promptly returned to the Board. And 247 CMR 3.05 sets a floor under the whole area: no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services as defined at M.G.L. c. 12, § 11I½, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts. A parallel provision for pharmacy support personnel appears at 247 CMR 8.08.

247 CMR 20.03 is worth reading closely, because its individual duties all share one period and differ only in their trigger. A licensee must maintain personal demographic information, including mailing address, phone number and email address, in the licensee's Massachusetts Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile, and must update that profile within 14 calendar days of a change to any of the three. On a change of name the licensee submits, within 14 calendar days, a sworn statement indicating that the licensee has changed name, together with a photocopy of a valid picture identification card and any other documentation the Board may require. Every individual licensed by the Board reports any arrest, pending criminal charge, or conviction within 14 calendar days, so the duty attaches at the arrest and does not wait for an adjudication. And each pharmacy and individual licensed by the Board reports any disciplinary action, as defined in 247 CMR 2.00, or loss of certification, within the same 14 calendar days. None of this waits for the next renewal, and an employer's personnel system is not the Board's record.

comparison_tables.title: What 247 CMR 3.05 does and does not do
columns: Answer on the regulation's own terms

worked_examples.scenario: An applicant sat NAPLEX and MPJE in the same month. She passed NAPLEX with 81% and failed MPJE with 71%. Fourteen months after the administration date of that original MPJE she submits an application to retake MPJE, reasoning that nothing in the regulation limits how many times she may sit it. What has the delay cost her?
steps: Fix the passing standard first: 247 CMR 3.01(5) requires a score of not less than 75% on each of NAPLEX and MPJE, so 81% is a pass and 71% is a fail.

Note that she is right about attempts. 247 CMR 3.01(6) allows re-examination on either or both examinations on a new application accompanied by all required fees, and states no cap on the number of attempts.

Now read the provision that actually bites. 247 CMR 3.01(7) required her to reapply to sit the failed examination within one year of the administration date of the original examination in order for both examination scores to be considered together.
Fourteen months is outside that year, so the two scores can no longer be considered together and the NAPLEX pass no longer carries.
Apply the stated consequence: if the applicant does not pass both NAPLEX and MPJE within the one-year period, the applicant must apply to retake both NAPLEX and MPJE.
worked_examples.resolution: She must retake NAPLEX as well as MPJE. The error the scenario invites is reading 247 CMR 3.01(7) as a limit on retakes; it is a shelf life for the score already earned, so what her delay destroyed is the examination she had already passed.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist licensed by examination in another state applies for Massachusetts licensure by reciprocity. NABP notifies her that she does not meet the requirements for licence transfer, and she believes NABP misread a lapsed licence in a third state as a disciplinary matter. A colleague tells her that NABP administers the transfer programme, so there is nothing to be done except start again. What are her options, and what will she still have to do if she succeeds?
steps: Identify NABP's role precisely. Under 247 CMR 3.02 the applicant submits a preliminary application to NABP, and NABP conducts the preliminary evaluation of the applicant's qualifications as agent of the Board.

Read who decides. 247 CMR 3.02(1)(b) gives the Board the final determination of any applicant's eligibility to be registered as a pharmacist by reciprocity, so NABP's notice is not the end of the matter.

Find the remedy the regulation actually provides. Under 247 CMR 3.02(1)(a) an applicant notified by NABP that she does not meet the requirements may request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision.

Keep the substantive element in view: 247 CMR 3.02 requires good standing in all states where the applicant holds a licence, so the third-state record still has to be resolved and not merely re-characterised.

Look ahead to what approval buys. A reciprocity application is valid for one year after the date of approval by NABP, and the requirements still include documentation of internship experience, a passing score of at least 75% on the MPJE, and personal appearance before the Board if requested.
worked_examples.resolution: She may ask the Board in writing to review the basis of NABP's decision, and if she succeeds she has one year from NABP approval and still has to pass the MPJE. The error the scenario invites is the colleague's: treating the preliminary evaluator as the decision-maker, and treating reciprocity as a route that brings an out-of-state jurisprudence result with it.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired on December 31st of an even-numbered year. He notices on March 15th following, pays the renewal fee, the back fees and the late fee that morning, and asks the manager whether he can take the afternoon shift while the Board processes it. A second pharmacist in the same store let her registration go for about 30 months and is asking the same question. Neither registration was ever suspended or revoked.
steps: Place the first pharmacist on the ladder. His lapse is more than 60 days but nowhere near two years, so 247 CMR 4.02(4) governs: he may apply for renewal on satisfying conditions imposed by the Board, which may include the completion of additional contact hours of continuing education.
Do not import the two-year consequence into the 60-day branch. The express requirement to take and pass the MPJE belongs to 247 CMR 4.02(5) and attaches to a failure to renew for more than two years.

Answer the shift question from 247 CMR 4.02(3): any practice of pharmacy after the expiration of the personal registration constitutes the unlicensed practice of pharmacy. The payment he made under 247 CMR 4.02(2) is a step in renewing, not a renewal.

Place the second pharmacist. Thirty months is more than two years, so under 247 CMR 4.02(5) she shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all other conditions determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal.

Check the qualifier both branches carry in their own text. 247 CMR 4.02(4) and (5) reach an applicant whose personal registration has not been suspended or revoked by the Board; a suspended or revoked registration takes a different route back, which this section does not cover.
worked_examples.resolution: Neither pharmacist may work until the registration has actually been renewed; the first faces Board-imposed conditions and the second must take and pass the MPJE first. The error the scenario invites is treating payment as reinstatement, with a second error close behind it: collapsing the 60-day and two-year branches into one undifferentiated idea of being lapsed.

worked_examples.scenario: A Massachusetts pharmacist marries and takes her spouse's surname, moves to a new mailing address, and in the same month is arrested and charged with a misdemeanour that is dismissed seven weeks later. While packing she also finds the original wallet card she had replaced with a duplicate two years earlier. She updates her employer's personnel system and plans to tell the Board about all of it on her next renewal application.
steps: Separate the two records. An employer's personnel system is not the Board's record; 247 CMR 20.03(1) puts the licensee's demographic information in the licensee's Massachusetts Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile.
Run each trigger against the same period. The change of mailing address requires her to update the on-line licensing profile within 14 calendar days under 247 CMR 20.03(1).

The change of name requires, within 14 calendar days, a sworn statement indicating that she has changed her name, together with a photocopy of a valid picture identification card and any other documentation the Board may require, under 247 CMR 20.03(2).

The arrest is itself reportable. 247 CMR 20.03(3) requires every individual licensed by the Board to report any arrest, pending criminal charge, or conviction within 14 calendar days, so the later dismissal does not retrospectively excuse a report that was already due.

Handle the recovered certificate on its own footing. Under 247 CMR 3.03, where an original certificate of licensure is recovered after a duplicate has been issued, the duplicate shall be promptly returned to the Board.
worked_examples.resolution: Three separate 14-calendar-day reports were due and the duplicate certificate should have gone back promptly. The error the scenario invites is the deferral to renewal, and behind it the assumption that an arrest becomes reportable only if it ripens into a conviction.

worked_examples.scenario: A pharmacist intends to stop practising and petitions the Board to place her licence on retired status; two years later she wants to come back. When she filed the petition her Massachusetts renewal was pending and she had disclosed an out-of-state disciplinary sanction imposed solely for dispensing medication for gender-affirming health care services that would have been lawful in Massachusetts and were consistent with good professional practice here. She assumed the sanction would sink the renewal, and that retiring would close the file either way.
steps: Test her eligibility for retired status against 247 CMR 3.04(2): the licence must not be surrendered, suspended or revoked at the time of the petition, and she must demonstrate to the Board's satisfaction an intent to retire permanently from active practice in the Commonwealth and in all other jurisdictions.
Read what retired status is and is not. 247 CMR 3.04(1) calls it a nondisciplinary status, and 247 CMR 3.04(3) provides that a licensee with retired status may not practise.

Address the return trip. 247 CMR 3.04(1) lets the Board decline to review any petition for reinstatement or return to current status from a licensee whose status has been changed to retired, so coming back is at the Board's discretion rather than hers.

Address the assumption that retiring closes the file. Nothing in 247 CMR 3.04 prevents the Board from initiating, pursuing or taking a disciplinary action against a licensee whose licence is in retired status.

Return to the renewal she was worried about. Under 247 CMR 3.05 no person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to discipline or another sanction arising from dispensing medication for gender-affirming health care services as defined at M.G.L. c. 12, § 11I½, so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts, and both qualifiers are satisfied on these facts.
worked_examples.resolution: Retirement was permanent in intent and reversible only at the Board's discretion, it never shielded her from discipline, and the sanction she was worried about could not have grounded a denial of the renewal in the first place. The error the scenario invites is reading nondisciplinary as protective, and reading any out-of-state sanction as automatically disqualifying.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An applicant for licensure by examination must be ______ years of age or older by ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 18; the scheduled date of the examination applied for, under 247 CMR 3.01(1)(a) and (2)(a).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: FPGEC certification satisfies both the degree requirement and the internship requirement on the examination pathway.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. It stands in for the accredited degree only. 247 CMR 3.01(2)(d) still requires a pharmacy internship completed in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1), in the same terms as 247 CMR 3.01(1)(c) uses on the accredited-degree pathway.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: The minimum passing score on each of NAPLEX and MPJE is ______, and the window to reapply for a failed examination is ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: not less than 75%; one year; the administration date of the original examination, under 247 CMR 3.01(5) and (7).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An applicant passed NAPLEX, failed MPJE, and reapplies fifteen months after the original MPJE administration date. Which examinations must she now take, and why?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Both NAPLEX and MPJE. 247 CMR 3.01(7) makes the one-year window the condition on which both scores are considered together, so once it has run the earlier NAPLEX pass no longer counts and the applicant must apply to retake both.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Which pathway and why: a pharmacist already licensed by examination in another state who wants to practise in Massachusetts.
retrieval_prompts.answer: Reciprocity under 247 CMR 3.02, because she can furnish proof of licensure by examination in another jurisdiction and of good standing in all states where she holds a licence. She still needs documented internship experience and a passing MPJE score of at least 75%.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: NABP's notification that an applicant does not meet the reciprocity requirements is the final decision on eligibility.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. NABP conducts the preliminary evaluation as agent of the Board. 247 CMR 3.02(1)(b) gives the Board the final determination, and 247 CMR 3.02(1)(a) lets the applicant request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An approved reciprocity application stays valid for ______, measured from ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: one year; the date of approval by NABP, under 247 CMR 3.02(1)(c).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: when the Board refuses to consider an incomplete licensure application, the fees are returned because nothing was really decided.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 3.01(8) lets the Board refuse to consider an application that has not been properly completed, and 247 CMR 3.01(9) makes all fees submitted in connection with an application reviewed and acted upon by the Board non-refundable.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Name the five things 247 CMR 3.01(3) requires of a completed application for examination.
retrieval_prompts.answer: It must be fully and correctly completed by the applicant, and include a recent passport-size photograph, a certified birth certificate or other sufficient proof of place and date of birth, written notification of a name change where there has been one, and payment of all required fees unless waived in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: Personal registrations expire on ______ of each ______ year, and must be renewed prior to ______.
retrieval_prompts.answer: December 31st; even-numbered; January 1st of the following year, under 247 CMR 4.02(1).

retrieval_prompts.prompt: A registration has been lapsed for 90 days and was never suspended or revoked. What does the regulation require, and what does it not require?
retrieval_prompts.answer: Renewal on satisfying conditions imposed by the Board, which may include additional contact hours of continuing education, under 247 CMR 4.02(4). It does not require the MPJE; that consequence attaches under 247 CMR 4.02(5) to a failure to renew for more than two years.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: True or false: retired status protects a licensee from Board discipline because the regulation calls it nondisciplinary.
retrieval_prompts.answer: False. 247 CMR 3.04(1) calls retired status nondisciplinary, but 247 CMR 3.04(4) preserves the Board's power to initiate, pursue or take disciplinary action against a licensee whose licence is in retired status.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: An original certificate of licensure turns up after a duplicate has been issued. Which one goes back to the Board, and how quickly?
Under 247 CMR 20.03 a licensee has ______ calendar days to report an arrest, and the duty attaches at ______ rather than at conviction.
retrieval_prompts.answer: 14; the arrest itself, because 247 CMR 20.03(3) reaches any arrest, pending criminal charge, or conviction.

retrieval_prompts.prompt: 247 CMR 3.05 bars denial of licensure or renewal for a protected-activity sanction only if two things are true. Name both.
retrieval_prompts.answer: The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts, and they are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts.

quick_review.text: Both examination pathways in 247 CMR 3.01(1) and (2) require age 18 by the scheduled examination date, a pharmacy internship in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1), and good moral character; only the academic credential differs.

FPGEC certification from NABP, an official copy of the certificate submitted to the Board and official NABP notification to the Board substitute for the accredited doctor of pharmacy degree, and for nothing else.
An applicant must pass both NAPLEX and MPJE with a score of not less than 75% on each, and may be re-examined on either or both on a new application with all required fees.
247 CMR 3.01(7) gives one year from the administration date of the original examination to reapply for the failed one; miss it and both examinations must be retaken.

Reciprocity requires licensure by examination elsewhere, good standing in all states where the applicant holds a licence, and a jurisdiction whose competency requirements equal Massachusetts requirements and which the Board recognises for reciprocity.

NABP conducts the preliminary reciprocity evaluation as agent of the Board; the Board makes the final determination, and an applicant rejected by NABP may ask the Board in writing to review the basis of that decision.

A completed examination application must be fully and correctly completed and carry a passport-size photograph, proof of place and date of birth, written notice of any name change, and all required fees unless waived in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B.
The Board may refuse to consider an improperly completed application, and fees on an application it has reviewed and acted upon are non-refundable.

Personal registrations expire on December 31st of each even-numbered year and must be renewed prior to January 1st of the following year; a registrant who missed the date may renew on paying the annual fee, applicable back fees and a late fee.

Any practice of pharmacy after expiration is the unlicensed practice of pharmacy; more than 60 days lapsed brings Board-imposed conditions, and more than two years lapsed brings the MPJE, each where the registration was not suspended or revoked.

Retired status is nondisciplinary and voluntary, bars practice, requires an intent to retire permanently in the Commonwealth and all other jurisdictions, and leaves the Board free both to decline a reinstatement petition and to discipline the retired licensee.

A duplicate certificate of licensure, the wallet card, is requested on a Board-approved form with the required documentation, and the duplicate is promptly returned to the Board if the original is recovered.

247 CMR 20.03 runs on 14 calendar days throughout: profile updates for mailing address, phone and email; a sworn statement and photo identification for a name change; any arrest, pending criminal charge or conviction; and any disciplinary action or loss of certification.

247 CMR 3.05 bars denial of initial licensure or renewal for a complaint, charge, conviction, judgment, discipline or other sanction arising from reproductive or gender-affirming health care services, provided the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice here.

decision_logic.condition: An applicant asks which licensure pathway applies.
decision_logic.action: Ask whether the applicant is already licensed by examination in another state or jurisdiction. If yes, the reciprocity route in 247 CMR 3.02 is available; if no, it is the examination route in 247 CMR 3.01.

decision_logic.condition: The applicant graduated from a college or school of pharmacy that is not ACPE-accredited or Board-approved.
decision_logic.action: Look for official FPGEC certification from NABP, an official copy of the certificate submitted to the Board and official NABP notification, and then check the internship, age and good moral character elements separately, because the certification replaces only the degree.

decision_logic.condition: An applicant failed one of the two examinations.
decision_logic.action: Date the original administration and count one year forward. Reapplication to sit the failed examination inside that year keeps both scores in play; outside it, both NAPLEX and MPJE must be retaken.

decision_logic.condition: NABP has told a reciprocity applicant that she does not qualify.
decision_logic.action: Do not treat that as final. The applicant may request in writing that the Board review the basis of NABP's decision, because the Board makes the final determination of eligibility.

decision_logic.condition: An application is submitted without one of the items 247 CMR 3.01(3) requires.
decision_logic.action: Expect the Board to be entitled to refuse to consider it, and do not expect the fees back once the Board has reviewed and acted upon it.

decision_logic.condition: A registrant wants to work while a late renewal is being processed.
decision_logic.action: Say no. Practice after the expiration of the personal registration is the unlicensed practice of pharmacy, and paying the annual, back and late fees is a step in renewing rather than a renewal.

decision_logic.condition: A personal registration has lapsed and was never suspended or revoked.
decision_logic.action: Measure the lapse. More than 60 days brings renewal on Board-imposed conditions, which may include additional continuing education contact hours; more than two years additionally requires taking and passing the MPJE. If the registration was suspended or revoked, neither branch applies and the route back lies outside this section.

decision_logic.condition: A licensee wants to stop practising without surrendering the licence.
decision_logic.action: Check that the licence is not surrendered, suspended or revoked, and that the intent to retire is permanent and covers all other jurisdictions, then petition for retired status; but treat the return to current status as discretionary with the Board and the Board's disciplinary authority as unaffected.

decision_logic.condition: An original certificate of licensure is found after a duplicate was issued.
decision_logic.action: Send the duplicate back to the Board promptly, and keep the original.

decision_logic.condition: Any of a licensee's reportable circumstances changes.
decision_logic.action: Start a 14-calendar-day clock. Mailing address, phone and email go into the Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile; a name change, an arrest or pending charge or conviction, and a disciplinary action or loss of certification are reported to the Board.

decision_logic.condition: A licensure or renewal file contains a sanction arising from reproductive or gender-affirming health care services.
decision_logic.action: Ask the two qualifying questions: would the services have been lawful in Massachusetts, and are they consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts. If both are satisfied, the sanction cannot be the basis for denying initial licensure or renewal.

exceptions.text: Fees required on a licensure application, on re-examination and on the reciprocity pathway are all payable unless waived in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112, § 1B.
The 60-day and two-year lapse branches in 247 CMR 4.02(4) and (5) apply only to an applicant whose personal registration has not been suspended or revoked by the Board.
Retired status carries no right of return: the Board may decline to review any petition for reinstatement or return to current status from a licensee whose status has been changed to retired.

The protection in 247 CMR 3.05 is conditional, not absolute; it holds only so long as the services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts.
FPGEC certification is an exception to the accredited-degree requirement only; the internship, age and good moral character elements are stated identically on both examination pathways.

Personal appearance before the Board is a reciprocity requirement only if requested, but the requirement to appear when asked is stated on both the accredited and the non-approved reciprocity branches.

timing_deadlines.event: Applicant reaches the minimum age for examination
timing_deadlines.timeframe: 18 years of age or older by the scheduled date of the examination applied for
timing_deadlines.consequence: An applicant who will not be 18 by that date is not eligible for that examination on either pathway.

timing_deadlines.event: Reapplication to sit an examination the applicant failed
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within one year of the administration date of the original examination
timing_deadlines.consequence: Reapplying inside the year keeps both examination scores considered together; outside it the applicant must apply to retake both NAPLEX and MPJE.

timing_deadlines.event: Validity of a reciprocity application approved by NABP
timing_deadlines.timeframe: One year after the date of approval by NABP
timing_deadlines.consequence: After a year the NABP approval no longer supports the application.

timing_deadlines.event: Expiration and renewal of a personal registration
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Expires December 31st of each even-numbered year; renewal is due prior to January 1st of the following year
timing_deadlines.consequence: Any practice of pharmacy after expiration constitutes the unlicensed practice of pharmacy and is subject to the penalties for it.

timing_deadlines.event: Failure to renew for more than 60 days, registration never suspended or revoked
timing_deadlines.consequence: Renewal only on satisfying conditions imposed by the Board, which may include the completion of additional contact hours of continuing education.

timing_deadlines.event: Failure to renew for more than two years, registration never suspended or revoked
timing_deadlines.timeframe: More than two years after expiration
timing_deadlines.consequence: The applicant shall take and pass the MPJE and meet all other conditions determined by the Board before the registration is renewed.

timing_deadlines.event: Change of mailing address, phone number or email address
timing_deadlines.timeframe: Within 14 calendar days of the change
timing_deadlines.consequence: The licensee must update the Massachusetts Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile; an employer's personnel record does not discharge the duty.
A sworn statement of the name change, a photocopy of a valid picture identification card and any other documentation the Board requires must be submitted.

timing_deadlines.event: Arrest, pending criminal charge or conviction of an individual licensee
timing_deadlines.consequence: The report is due to the Board on the arrest itself, so a later dismissal does not excuse a report that has already fallen due.

timing_deadlines.event: Disciplinary action as defined in 247 CMR 2.00, or loss of certification
timing_deadlines.consequence: The report is due to the Board from each pharmacy and individual licensed by the Board.

timing_deadlines.event: Recovery of an original certificate of licensure after a duplicate has been issued
timing_deadlines.consequence: The duplicate, not the original, shall be returned to the Board.

forms_records.text: The completed application for examination carries a recent passport-size photograph showing the applicant's likeness, a certified birth certificate or other sufficient proof of place and date of birth, written notification of any name change to the Board or the Board's designee, and payment of all required fees.

On the non-approved-school examination pathway the record consists of an official copy of the applicant's FPGEC certificate submitted to the Board together with official notification of the certification received by the Board from NABP.
The reciprocity file starts with a preliminary application for licence transfer submitted to NABP and goes on to documentation of internship experience and a passing MPJE score of at least 75%.
Re-examination is requested by a new application for examination to the Board or a Board-approved testing service, accompanied by payment of all required fees.
A duplicate certificate of licensure, the wallet card, is requested on a Board-approved form with the required documentation.

The licensee's Massachusetts Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile is the record of the licensee's mailing address, phone number and email address, and a name change is documented by a sworn statement plus a photocopy of a valid picture identification card.

A request for retired status takes the form of a petition to the Board demonstrating, to the Board's satisfaction, an intent to retire permanently from active practice in the Commonwealth and in all other jurisdictions.

role_duties.duty: Meet the age, credential, internship and good moral character elements before the scheduled examination date, and pass both NAPLEX and MPJE with not less than 75% on each.

Reapply to sit the failed examination within one year of the administration date of the original examination, on a new application with all required fees, if both scores are to be considered together.

Submit the preliminary application to NABP, produce documentation of internship experience and a passing MPJE score of at least 75%, remain in good standing in all states where a licence is held, and appear personally before the Board if requested.

role_duties.role: NABP, as agent of the Board
role_duties.duty: Conduct the preliminary evaluation of a reciprocity applicant's qualifications and notify the applicant of the result, without deciding eligibility.
Make the final determination of any applicant's eligibility for reciprocity and, on written request, review the basis of NABP's decision.
Decide whether to consider an application that has not been properly completed, and retain the fees on any application it has reviewed and acted upon.
Set the conditions on which a registration lapsed more than 60 days may be renewed, and the further conditions accompanying the MPJE where the lapse exceeds two years.
Refrain from denying initial licensure or renewal on the basis of a sanction arising from reproductive or gender-affirming health care services that satisfy the two Massachusetts qualifiers.
Renew prior to January 1st following the December 31st expiry of an even-numbered year, and stop practising while the registration is expired.

Keep mailing address, phone number and email address current in the Department of Public Health on-line licensing profile, and report a name change, an arrest or pending criminal charge or conviction, and any disciplinary action or loss of certification, each within 14 calendar days.
Return the duplicate to the Board promptly if the original certificate of licensure is recovered.
Refrain from practice, and treat any return to current status as a matter the Board may decline to review.

common_traps.text: Treating FPGEC certification as a general exemption. It substitutes for the accredited degree only; the internship, the age element and good moral character are stated in the same terms on both examination pathways.
Reading 247 CMR 3.01(7) as a limit on the number of retakes. It is a one-year linkage window, and what expires with it is the score the applicant has already passed.
Assuming reciprocity waives the MPJE because the applicant already passed a jurisprudence examination elsewhere. A passing score of at least 75% on the MPJE is a stated reciprocity requirement.
Treating NABP's preliminary decision as final, or as appealable only to NABP. The Board makes the final determination and will review the basis of NABP's decision on written request.
Expecting a refund when the Board declines to consider an incomplete application. Refusing to consider it is still reviewing and acting upon it, and the fees are non-refundable.
Treating the payment of renewal, back and late fees as a restoration of the right to practise. Practice after expiration is unlicensed practice until the registration is actually renewed.

Collapsing the 60-day and two-year lapse branches, or importing the MPJE requirement into the shorter one. The 60-day branch produces Board-imposed conditions that may include additional continuing education contact hours; only the two-year branch names the MPJE.
Reading nondisciplinary as protective. Retired status neither permits practice nor prevents the Board from initiating, pursuing or taking disciplinary action.
Returning the recovered original certificate instead of the duplicate. The regulation sends the duplicate back, promptly, and lets the registrant keep the original.

Saving reportable events for the renewal application, or waiting for a criminal case to conclude. Every individual duty in 247 CMR 20.03 runs on 14 calendar days, and the criminal duty attaches at the arrest.

Reading 247 CMR 3.05 as an unconditional bar on considering out-of-state sanctions. The protection depends on the services having been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with standards for good professional practice here.
